title: The Softest Hand of All
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
When something makes my eyes go wet
And I can't tell you why,
There is a hand that finds my face
And wipes the tears I cry.

[Chorus]
The softest hand of all is near,
So close I need not call;
He counts each tear and dries each one,
The softest hand of all.

[Verse 2]
He sees the tear I hide inside
And every one I show;
He knows the sad I cannot say,
He hears me crying low.

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
He whispers, "It is all right now,"
As gentle as the rain;
He turns my crying into song
And holds me close again.

[Chorus]

[Verse 4]
And someday every tear will end
On every single face;
No crying in that morning light,
Just gladness in its place.

[Chorus]
mood: Tear-drying music. A slow rocking sway under the voice, the movement of an arm around a child who has just stopped crying rather than one still in it. A cello leaning in beneath a fingerpicked guitar, answering the end of each line the way someone murmurs I know, I know. It begins damp and unsteady and dries out as it goes, each verse sitting lower and looser than the one before, until the last line is barely more than breathing.
